regras/cenas-e-conflitos/acoes/aguardar.title: Wait
regras/cenas-e-conflitos/acoes/aguardar.summary: Acting right away is not always the best choice. When using Wait, the character gives up acting at that moment to wait for a better opportunity during the Scene. Wait can be used in two ways: Delay the Turn, waiting to…
regras/cenas-e-conflitos/acoes/aguardar.text:
Acting right away is not always the best choice.
When using Wait, the character gives up acting at that moment to wait for a better opportunity during the Scene.
Wait can be used in two ways:
Delay the Turn, waiting to take the Turn later.
Ready an Action, choosing in advance what they will do if a given situation happens.
Although both represent waiting before acting, each works differently.
Delay the Turn
When they Delay the Turn, the character gives up acting in their current Initiative position and keeps waiting for a chance to rejoin the Turn order.
Delaying the Turn is not an Action: you decide to delay when your Turn comes up, before it begins. Start-of-Turn effects, such as those of some Capabilities, happen only when you actually act.
From that moment on, the player can choose a later Turn in the Round to act, and takes their full Turn.
Joining a Turn
When the character decides to stop waiting, they act immediately after the current Turn ends, whether it belongs to an ally, an opponent or an NPC. This rule applies to player characters and NPCs alike.
Current Turn → Waiting character
This becomes the character's new Initiative position for the rest of the Scene.
If more than one character wants to act after the same Turn, they act in their original Initiative order.
If the character does not decide to act by the end of the Round, they automatically act last in that Round, and that becomes their new Initiative position.
Example
The starting Initiative order is:
Amara → Dorian → Guard → Iselle
On Amara's Turn, she decides to Delay the Turn.
During Dorian's Turn, Amara decides to act. Dorian finishes his Turn and Amara acts immediately after, before the Guard:
Dorian → Amara → Guard → Iselle
If Amara had instead decided to act during the Guard's Turn, the Guard would finish their Turn first and Amara would act immediately after:
Dorian → Guard → Amara → Iselle
In both cases, this becomes Amara's new Initiative position for the rest of the Scene.
Ready an Action
When they Ready an Action, the character uses their Action on their own Turn to set in advance something they will do if a given situation happens.
To do so, the player must declare:
which Action will be taken;
which trigger will set off that Action.
For example:
"If the guard comes through the door, I start a Confront against them."
"If anyone gets close to the lever, I run to it."
The trigger must be clear and represent something that can be objectively identified during the Scene.
When the Action happens
When the declared trigger happens, the character can immediately take the Action they readied.
The trigger happens first and, as soon as it occurs, the readied Action is taken before the character who set off the trigger carries on with other activities in their Turn.
Once it is resolved, the interrupted Turn continues as usual, if still possible.
Action set in advance
The Action taken must be the one declared when it was readied.
The player can decide not to take the Action when its trigger happens, but cannot swap it at that moment for a different Action.
If they want to do something else, they must wait for their next Turn as usual.
Action requirements
When the trigger happens, the character still needs to be able to take the readied Action.
All the usual requirements still apply, including reach, equipment, position and any other limitations.
For example, readying a Confront against someone does not allow taking it if the target is out of reach when the trigger happens.
If the readied Action involves moving, the character uses the Movement they did not spend on their Turn. If the readied Action is Run, the extra squares are added to that remaining Movement.
Duration
A readied Action stays available until the start of the character's next Turn.
If the trigger does not happen before then, the readied Action is lost.
On the new Turn, the character can act normally or use their Action again to ready another.
Initiative
Unlike Delay the Turn, Readying an Action does not change the character's Initiative position.
The character keeps their usual position in the following Rounds, no matter when their readied Action is taken.
Example
The Initiative order is:
Amara → Guard → Dorian
During her Turn, Amara declares:
"I ready a Confront. If the Guard comes through the door, I attack them."
Amara uses her Action to ready this response.
On the Guard's Turn, they move and come through the door. Amara's trigger happens.
Before the Guard carries on with their Turn, Amara takes the readied Confront.
Once the Confront is resolved, the Guard carries on with their Turn as usual, if they still can.
In the following Round, Amara keeps her original Initiative position.
regras/cenas-e-conflitos/acoes/aguardar.html:
Acting right away is not always the best choice.

When using Wait, the character gives up acting at that moment to wait for a better opportunity during the Scene.

Wait can be used in two ways:

  • Delay the Turn, waiting to take the Turn later.
  • Ready an Action, choosing in advance what they will do if a given situation happens.

Although both represent waiting before acting, each works differently.

Delay the Turn

When they Delay the Turn, the character gives up acting in their current Initiative position and keeps waiting for a chance to rejoin the Turn order.

Delaying the Turn is not an Action: you decide to delay when your Turn comes up, before it begins. Start-of-Turn effects, such as those of some Capabilities, happen only when you actually act.

From that moment on, the player can choose a later Turn in the Round to act, and takes their full Turn.

Joining a Turn

When the character decides to stop waiting, they act immediately after the current Turn ends, whether it belongs to an ally, an opponent or an NPC. This rule applies to player characters and NPCs alike.

Current Turn → Waiting character

This becomes the character's new Initiative position for the rest of the Scene.

If more than one character wants to act after the same Turn, they act in their original Initiative order.

If the character does not decide to act by the end of the Round, they automatically act last in that Round, and that becomes their new Initiative position.

Example

The starting Initiative order is:

Amara → Dorian → Guard → Iselle

On Amara's Turn, she decides to Delay the Turn.

During Dorian's Turn, Amara decides to act. Dorian finishes his Turn and Amara acts immediately after, before the Guard:

Dorian → Amara → Guard → Iselle

If Amara had instead decided to act during the Guard's Turn, the Guard would finish their Turn first and Amara would act immediately after:

Dorian → Guard → Amara → Iselle

In both cases, this becomes Amara's new Initiative position for the rest of the Scene.

Ready an Action

When they Ready an Action, the character uses their Action on their own Turn to set in advance something they will do if a given situation happens.

To do so, the player must declare:

  • which Action will be taken;
  • which trigger will set off that Action.

For example:

"If the guard comes through the door, I start a Confront against them."

"If anyone gets close to the lever, I run to it."

The trigger must be clear and represent something that can be objectively identified during the Scene.

When the Action happens

When the declared trigger happens, the character can immediately take the Action they readied.

The trigger happens first and, as soon as it occurs, the readied Action is taken before the character who set off the trigger carries on with other activities in their Turn.

Once it is resolved, the interrupted Turn continues as usual, if still possible.

Action set in advance

The Action taken must be the one declared when it was readied.

The player can decide not to take the Action when its trigger happens, but cannot swap it at that moment for a different Action.

If they want to do something else, they must wait for their next Turn as usual.

Action requirements

When the trigger happens, the character still needs to be able to take the readied Action.

All the usual requirements still apply, including reach, equipment, position and any other limitations.

For example, readying a Confront against someone does not allow taking it if the target is out of reach when the trigger happens.

If the readied Action involves moving, the character uses the Movement they did not spend on their Turn. If the readied Action is Run, the extra squares are added to that remaining Movement.

Duration

A readied Action stays available until the start of the character's next Turn.

If the trigger does not happen before then, the readied Action is lost.

On the new Turn, the character can act normally or use their Action again to ready another.

Initiative

Unlike Delay the Turn, Readying an Action does not change the character's Initiative position.

The character keeps their usual position in the following Rounds, no matter when their readied Action is taken.

Example

The Initiative order is:

Amara → Guard → Dorian

During her Turn, Amara declares:

"I ready a Confront. If the Guard comes through the door, I attack them."

Amara uses her Action to ready this response.

On the Guard's Turn, they move and come through the door. Amara's trigger happens.

Before the Guard carries on with their Turn, Amara takes the readied Confront.

Once the Confront is resolved, the Guard carries on with their Turn as usual, if they still can.

In the following Round, Amara keeps her original Initiative position.

regras/cenas-e-conflitos/zonas.title: Zones
regras/cenas-e-conflitos/zonas.summary: A Zone represents an effect that occupies an area and affects the creatures inside it. The rule or Capability that creates a Zone sets its shape, size, range, position, duration, effects and, when applicable, its Damage…
regras/cenas-e-conflitos/zonas.text:
A Zone represents an effect that occupies an area and affects the creatures inside it.
The rule or Capability that creates a Zone sets its shape, size, range, position, duration, effects and, when applicable, its Damage and Damage Type.
By default, a Zone affects every creature inside it, including the allies of whoever created it. A creature whose space takes up more than one square is affected only once by the same Zone.
Shapes
Zone shapes use the grid as Movement does: a diagonal counts as 1 square. In the diagrams, C is whoever creates the Zone, ■ is an affected square, ◆ is the point of origin (also affected) and · is outside the Zone.
Burst N
Every square within N squares of a point of origin, chosen within the source's range. A Burst N forms a square with sides of 2N + 1. If the origin is the square of whoever creates the Zone, they are affected too.
Burst 1 and Burst 2:
```
· · · · · ■ ■ ■ ■ ■
· ■ ■ ■ · ■ ■ ■ ■ ■
· ■ ◆ ■ · ■ ■ ◆ ■ ■
· ■ ■ ■ · ■ ■ ■ ■ ■
· · · · · ■ ■ ■ ■ ■
```
Blast N
A square of N × N squares adjacent to whoever creates the Zone, in any direction, including diagonally. Whoever creates the Blast is not affected by it.
Blast 3 forward and diagonally:
```
■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ·
■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ·
■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ·
· C · · · · C
```
Line N
N squares in a straight line, horizontal, vertical or diagonal, starting from a square adjacent to whoever creates the Zone. Whoever creates the Line is not affected by it.
Line 4 horizontally and Line 3 diagonally:
```
C ■ ■ ■ ■ · · · ■
· · ■ ·
· ■ · ·
C · · ·
```
A creature that takes up more than one square measures the Blast and the Line from any square it occupies (see Size). The source can use another shape, as long as it describes it.
Damage Zones
When a creature is hit by a damage Zone, it makes a test of:
Agility + Acrobatics
The rule or Capability that created the Zone can set a different Dice Pool.
A creature that cannot resist follows the Target without a Response rule: its result counts as 1 Success.
Each Success on the test is applied as follows:
while there is aggravated damage, the Success converts 1 point of that damage to superficial;
once all the damage has been converted, each remaining Success removes 1 point of superficial damage.
Example
A creature is hit by a Damage 4 Zone.
Successes Damage taken 
0 4 aggravated 
2 2 aggravated and 2 superficial 
4 4 superficial 
5 3 superficial 
8 or more no damage 
Interactions
A Zone is neither an Attack nor a Confront. The Accept the Confront, Defend and Dodge Responses are not used.
Resisting a Zone is not Dodging. Bonuses, penalties and replacements specific to Dodge do not apply, unless a rule says otherwise.
Resisting a Zone does not move the creature.
Base Absorption and the Absorption granted by armor do not apply to a Zone's damage.
Resistances and Vulnerabilities to the Zone's Damage Type and Material are added together, as in Effective Absorption. A positive total converts that many points of aggravated damage to superficial before the test's Successes are applied; a negative total increases the Zone's Damage.
Immunity to the Zone's Damage Type or Material prevents the damage entirely.
Duration
A Zone can be instant or persistent.
Instant: resolves its effect as soon as it is created and then disappears.
Persistent: stays in place for the duration set by the rule or Capability that created it. That source also sets when the Zone affects a creature, such as on entering it or starting the Turn inside it. The same persistent Zone affects each creature at most once per Round.

regras/cenas-e-conflitos/iluminacao.title: Lighting
regras/cenas-e-conflitos/iluminacao.summary: The Lighting of a place sets how much can be seen there. It affects rolls that depend on seeing something, such as attacking, responding to an Attack, noticing or searching. The Narrator sets the lighting of each area…
regras/cenas-e-conflitos/iluminacao.text:
The Lighting of a place sets how much can be seen there. It affects rolls that depend on seeing something, such as attacking, responding to an Attack, noticing or searching.
The Narrator sets the lighting of each area.
Lighting Effect Examples 
Bright none daylight, a well-lit room 
Dim -2 dice on Perception tests that depend on sight; Attacks are not affected dusk, moonlight, the edge of a torch's light, light fog 
Dark whoever is in the Dark cannot be seen: -4 dice on every roll that depends on seeing that creature or object, including Attacks, responses to a Confront and Perception a moonless night, a cave or cellar with no light at all 
The penalty uses the lighting of the place where what you are trying to see is: the target of an Attack, the attacker you are responding to, the creature you are trying to notice or the object you are searching for. Whoever is in the Dark attacks someone in the light without a penalty, and whoever is in the light loses 4 dice to respond. If both are in the Dark, both lose 4 dice.
Darkvision
A creature with Darkvision, up to its range, treats Dim as Bright and Dark as Dim.
Supernatural Darkness
Supernatural darkness, such as darkness created by magic, counts as Dark, and not even Darkvision sees through it.
Light Sources
Light sources are in the Item Catalog. A light source makes the area around it Bright up to its radius, and Dim for the same radius beyond that.
Source Bright Dim beyond that 
Candle 1 square +1 square 
Torch 4 squares +4 squares 
Lantern 6 squares +6 squares

regras/movimento/movimento.title: Moving
regras/movimento/movimento.summary: This section gathers the movement rules used mainly during Tactical Scenes.
regras/movimento/movimento.text:
This section gathers the movement rules used mainly during Tactical Scenes.
Rules
Movement — standard movement, terrain and special movement.
Run — increase the distance covered during the Turn.
Jump — horizontal and vertical jumps.
Relations
Movement happens within the structure of Scenes and Conflicts and usually goes along with the character's Action.
regras/movimento/movimento.html:
This section gathers the movement rules used mainly during Tactical Scenes.

Rules

  • Movement — standard movement, terrain and special movement.
  • Run — increase the distance covered during the Turn.
  • Jump — horizontal and vertical jumps.

Relations

Movement happens within the structure of Scenes and Conflicts and usually goes along with the character's Action.

regras/movimento/movimentacao.title: Movement
regras/movimento/movimentacao.summary: During their Turn, a character can move across the battlefield using their Movement. By default, every character has a base Movement of 6 squares per Turn. Base Movement: 6 squares. When you need to express distances in…
regras/movimento/movimentacao.text:
During their Turn, a character can move across the battlefield using their Movement.
By default, every character has a base Movement of 6 squares per Turn.
Base Movement: 6 squares
When you need to express distances in physical units, use 1 square = 5 feet = 1.5 meters. The conversion is only a narrative reference.
Effects that reduce or increase a character's Movement change their base Movement. While the effect lasts, every rule that uses base Movement uses the modified value. Apply halving first, then additions and subtractions. Movement never goes below 0.
Movement can be used before and after the Action, and split between the two as the character prefers.
Moving Around
Each square moved costs 1 point of Movement.
Moving diagonally also costs only 1 point of Movement. Astra does not use extra costs for diagonal movement.
A character can move through a square occupied by an ally (without staying in it), but not through a square occupied by any other creature.
Difficult Terrain
Certain spaces can count as Difficult Terrain, representing surfaces or obstacles that slow movement down.
Each square of Difficult Terrain costs 2 points of Movement to cross.
For example, a character with 6 points of Movement could normally cross 6 squares, but only 3 squares if the whole path were Difficult Terrain.
Movement and Enemies
Moving out of an enemy's reach does not, by default, provoke Attacks or other penalties.
Certain Capabilities or effects can create exceptions to this rule, letting a character punish or interfere with their opponents' movement.
Forced Movement
Forced movement is any movement another character or an effect imposes on a character, such as that of the Reposition Maneuver, a shield's Repel, the Displace Mastery or the dragging of a grapple.
It does not spend the moved character's Movement, happens even with Movement 0 and does not provoke effects that react to movement, such as the Sentinel's Opportunity Attack. Obstacles and edges follow the rules of Reposition.
Special Movement
Special Movement is any form of movement different from the character's ordinary movement on land.
This includes situations such as swimming, climbing, crawling, squeezing through tight spaces or any other form of locomotion that requires effort, technique or conditions different from normal movement.
Each square covered using Special Movement costs 2 points of Movement.
1 square of Special Movement = 2 points of Movement
Costs add up. A square of Difficult Terrain crossed with Special Movement costs 4 points of Movement.
Normally, swimming and climbing do not require a roll. When the risk, pressure or difficulty of the situation calls for a test, the standard Pool is Strength + Athletics. Long trials of endurance or exhaustion may call for a Vigor + Determination test, depending on the situation.
Flight
Flight does not use the Special Movement rules.
How a character flies, their speed, limitations, costs and other properties are set directly by the Capability, equipment, effect or other source that grants that ability.
This way, different forms of flight can work in different ways, depending on their origin.
Falling
A creature that falls takes 1 point of Bludgeoning damage per 2 squares of height, with no test, up to a maximum of 10 (from 20 squares on). Absorption does not apply to falling damage. The damage is aggravated, like any damage.
Falling damage = height in squares ÷ 2 (maximum 10)
Whoever takes falling damage ends up Prone.
Whoever jumps down on purpose subtracts the height of their Vertical Jump from the height of the fall.
For example, a creature pushed off a 5-square wall takes 2 damage and ends up Prone. A 15-meter fall (10 squares) deals 5 damage.
Jumping
Jumping is part of Movement: each square jumped costs 1 point, without using the Action. See Jump.

regras/movimento/correr.title: Run
regras/movimento/correr.summary: When using the Run Action, the character gets additional Movement points equal to their base Movement for that Turn. With the default base of 6, that is +6, for a total of 12; with a base of 8, it is +8, for a total of…
regras/movimento/correr.text:
When using the Run Action, the character gets additional Movement points equal to their base Movement for that Turn. With the default base of 6, that is +6, for a total of 12; with a base of 8, it is +8, for a total of 16.
Running needs no test. The character can choose to Run after having already moved: the additional points are added to whatever they still have that Turn.
Run effects stack: a character who gets Run from a Capability and also uses the Run Action adds both.

regras/movimento/saltar.title: Jump
regras/movimento/saltar.summary: Jumping is part of Movement: the character jumps horizontally or vertically while moving, without using their Action. Each square jumped costs 1 point of Movement, like walking. The base distance of the Jump is equal to…
regras/movimento/saltar.text:
Jumping is part of Movement: the character jumps horizontally or vertically while moving, without using their Action. Each square jumped costs 1 point of Movement, like walking.
The base distance of the Jump is equal to half of the character's Strength, rounded down.
Base Jump distance = Strength ÷ 2 (rounded down)
Run-up
The character can run before jumping to get a Run-up. Each square covered in a straight line, right before the jump, adds +1 square to the distance. These squares also cost Movement as usual.
The maximum Run-up that can be used is equal to the character's Athletics, with a minimum of 1 square.
Maximum Run-up = Athletics (minimum 1)
The character does not have to use all of the available Run-up. Only the squares actually covered before the Jump are added to the distance.
Jump distance = half of Strength + Run-up
A Jump does not require a roll. As long as the intended distance is within the character's limit and they have enough Movement, they can make it.
Vertical Jump
The same rules can be used to determine the height reached by a Jump.
In that case, the maximum height the character can reach is equal to half of the calculated distance, rounded down.
Jump height = Jump distance ÷ 2 (rounded down)
Example
A character has:
Strength 4
Athletics 3
Their base Jump distance is 2 squares.
Since they have Athletics 3, they can use up to 3 squares of Run-up. If they cover the 3 squares in a straight line before jumping, they can reach:
2 + 3 = 5 squares
The Run-up and the jump together cost 8 points of Movement. With the base Movement of 6, they need to Run to make the whole jump in the same Turn; without Running, they can use 1 square of Run-up and jump 3 squares (4 points).
On a Vertical Jump with the same 3 squares of Run-up, they would reach 2 squares of height.

regras/equipamentos/equipamentos.title: Equipment
regras/equipamentos/equipamentos.summary: Equipment is the objects characters carry and use, whether to attack, protect themselves or carry out other tasks. The Astra core currently organizes equipment into five types: Weapons — equipment used to attack. Armor…
regras/equipamentos/equipamentos.text:
Equipment is the objects characters carry and use, whether to attack, protect themselves or carry out other tasks.
The Astra core currently organizes equipment into five types:
Weapons — equipment used to attack.
Armor — equipment used for protection.
Shields — equipment used for defense.
Consumables — Drugs and alchemicals, which are spent in a single use.
Common items — everyday objects, such as backpacks, ropes and tools.
The equipment available in the core is gathered in:
Weapon Catalog;
Armor Catalog;
Shield Catalog;
Consumable Catalog;
Item Catalog.
New equipment types may be added in the future, through specific modules or settings.
Value
All equipment has a Value, used to compare prices and build budgets. Value is an abstract number and may have decimals; the setting decides the currency's name, its availability and the buying rules.
Use during scenes
Switching Equipment — drawing, stowing and switching equipment during the Tactical Scene.
Scenes and Conflicts — rules for confrontations and other tactical decisions.
Load
The weight of equipment is not measured in kilograms. In Astra, the space an item takes up is measured by its Load, a whole number. This applies equally to weapons, armor, shields, Consumables and common items. Very small items have Load 0 (see Item Catalog).
Maximum Load
A character's Maximum Load is the total Load they can carry without penalties. Its standard formula is:
5 + Strength
A Backpack increases Maximum Load by 2.

have their base Movement cut in half (see Movement);
suffer -2 dice on rolls that use a Physical Attribute.

regras/equipamentos/equipamentos.html:
Equipment is the objects characters carry and use, whether to attack, protect themselves or carry out other tasks.

The Astra core currently organizes equipment into five types:

  • Weapons — equipment used to attack.
  • Armor — equipment used for protection.
  • Shields — equipment used for defense.
  • Consumables — Drugs and alchemicals, which are spent in a single use.
  • Common items — everyday objects, such as backpacks, ropes and tools.

The equipment available in the core is gathered in:

  • Weapon Catalog;
  • Armor Catalog;
  • Shield Catalog;
  • Consumable Catalog;
  • Item Catalog.

New equipment types may be added in the future, through specific modules or settings.

Value

All equipment has a Value, used to compare prices and build budgets. Value is an abstract number and may have decimals; the setting decides the currency's name, its availability and the buying rules.

Use during scenes

  • Switching Equipment — drawing, stowing and switching equipment during the Tactical Scene.
  • Scenes and Conflicts — rules for confrontations and other tactical decisions.

Load

The weight of equipment is not measured in kilograms. In Astra, the space an item takes up is measured by its Load, a whole number. This applies equally to weapons, armor, shields, Consumables and common items. Very small items have Load 0 (see Item Catalog).

Maximum Load

A character's Maximum Load is the total Load they can carry without penalties. Its standard formula is:

5 + Strength

A Backpack increases Maximum Load by 2.

Strength is the Load Attribute by default. Capabilities and other rules can replace it in this formula. When that happens, Maximum Load is recalculated immediately from the new Attribute, without changing Strength tests or other rules.

Overload

Carrying more than the Maximum Load leaves the character in Overload. While in Overload, they:

  • have their base Movement cut in half (see Movement);
  • suffer -2 dice on rolls that use a Physical Attribute.

Above double the Maximum Load, the character cannot move while carrying everything.

Overload ends as soon as the Load is back within the limit.

regras/equipamentos/armas.text:
Weapons are equipment used to attack, usually in a Confront.
Each weapon is described by the following fields:
Field Description 
Name the weapon's name 
Damage a fixed modifier (1, 2, 3…) added to the damage in a Confront 
Damage Type the type of damage the weapon deals — Slashing, Piercing, Bludgeoning, Fire, etc. (see Damage Types) 
Grip how the weapon is held (see Grip) 
Reach the reach, in squares, at which the weapon can hit its targets 
Other Properties the weapon's Use Properties (see Use) 
Mastery the effect only those who have mastered the weapon can use (see Mastery) 
Material the category of the weapon's material (see Material) 
Load how much of the Maximum Load it takes 
Value the weapon's cost 
A weapon's Damage is the weapon bonus applied in a Confront, added to the Margin of Successes (see Confront).
The weapons available in the core are in the Weapon Catalog.
Unarmed
Every character has a natural weapon, Unarmed: punches, kicks, elbows and the body itself.
Field Value 
Damage +0 
Damage Type Bludgeoning 
Reach 1 
Load 0 
Unarmed has the Natural Origin and the Organic Material: it is always available, does not need to be equipped and does not take up the hands. It also cannot be removed, sold or lost. When the character attacks with no weapon in hand, they use Unarmed.
By default, Unarmed damage is superficial (see Damage Severity). Since its Damage is +0, a tie in an unarmed Confront deals no damage. Capabilities can change these traits when their effect expressly says so.
Properties
A weapon's Properties are organized into five categories. Every weapon has exactly one Origin and one Material; the Grip, Use and Mastery properties are optional and can be combined as the weapon's entry says.
Origin (required, one per weapon)
Crafted — a weapon made to be used as a weapon. This is the default origin.
Improvised — an ordinary object used as a weapon.
Natural — a weapon that is part of the body, such as fists, claws, fangs or tails. It is always available: it does not need to be equipped, does not take up the hands and cannot be the target of the Disarm Maneuver. Unarmed is Natural.
Material (required, one per weapon)
Material represents a category that matters for defenses, rather than telling apart every common raw material.
Material Covers 
Organic Body, flesh, claws, fangs, bones and shells 
Wood Common wood and other plant materials used in weapons 
Stone Rock, flint, obsidian and common minerals 
Common metal Iron, steel, bronze, copper and other common alloys 
Silver Special material, with its own interaction with defenses 
Meteorite Special material, with its own interaction with defenses 
Special materials is an organizing category, not a selectable option. Each special material has its own entry. Every weapon still has exactly one Material: Silver and Meteorite do not also count as Common metal.
Material is considered together with the Damage Type when applying Resistances, Vulnerabilities and Immunities. Resistances and Vulnerabilities to the Type and the Material are added together when calculating Effective Absorption; Immunity to either one ignores all the damage. For now, these Material values are set directly on characters and creatures.
Grip (optional)
Light — a nimble, balanced weapon. It has no effect of its own; some Capabilities require Light weapons, such as Ambidextrous.
Two-handed — a weapon that must be held in both hands to be used.
Flexible — a weapon that can be used in one hand or both. Held in both hands, it gets +1 Damage.
Attached — a weapon fixed to the body or the armor, which does not take up the hand and cannot be the target of the Disarm Maneuver. It only attacks when the hand it is attached to holds nothing. Each hand has at most one Attached weapon.
Use (optional)
Heavy — Attacks made with this weapon use Strength instead of Agility, keeping the Skill set by the kind of Attack. A Heavy melee weapon uses Strength + Fighting; a Heavy shooting weapon uses Strength + Shooting. This replacement is mandatory, adds no dice or Damage. Heavy changes only Attacks: it does not change the Pools of Maneuvers made with the weapon. A Capability that expressly sets the Attack's Attribute always takes precedence over Heavy.
Thrown (value) — a weapon that can be thrown as a ranged Attack. The Property always comes with a value, which gives the weapon's throwing Range in squares — for example, Thrown (6) means the weapon can be thrown up to 6 squares. Thrown Attacks use Strength + Throwing, unless explicitly replaced. The weapon's Reach field still applies to its melee use. In a Confront, the weapon can be used to Accept the Confront against a ranged attacker, as long as they are within the throwing Range.
Versatile (damage type) — a weapon with a second Damage Type, given in the Property. The attacker chooses which one to use on each Attack. For example, a Piercing weapon with Versatile (Slashing).
Nonlethal — the weapon's damage is always superficial (see Damage Severity). To deal aggravated damage with it, the attacker suffers -2 dice on the Attack.
Maneuver (Reposition, Trip or Disarm) — the weapon can be used to perform the given Maneuver up to the weapon's Reach, instead of requiring physical contact. The Maneuver gets no bonus from the weapon and keeps its own Pool; the Heavy property does not change that Pool either.
Ammunition (type) — a shooting weapon that fires the given ammunition, such as Ammunition (arrows) (see Item Catalog). Each shot spends 1 ammunition, whether starting a Confront or Accepting the Confront; without ammunition, the weapon cannot fire. Drawing the ammunition is part of the Attack. On the Attack, the ammunition's Material applies, not the weapon's. At the end of the Scene, if there is time to search, the character recovers half the ammunition spent, rounded down.
Loading — the weapon fires at most once per Round.
Charge — if the character moved at least 3 squares in a straight line to the target this Turn, right before the Attack, the Attack gets +1 Damage.
Guard — while wielding the weapon, the character gets +1 die when they Dodge. Two weapons with Guard do not add up.
Mastery (optional, at most one per weapon)
Mastery is an effect characteristic of the weapon's model, which only shows itself in the hands of someone who has mastered it. It belongs to the weapon, but can only be used by a character who has mastered that weapon (see Mastering a Weapon). Anyone who has not mastered it uses the weapon normally, without the Mastery.
Each weapon has at most one Mastery. A Mastery can create effects on winning an Attack, change a specific interaction or represent an advantage that does not fit the structural categories above.
Techniques the character has learned still belong to Capabilities. The Mastery describes what the weapon does in the hands of someone who has mastered it; a Capability describes what the character knows how to do.
A Mastery that says on winning an Attack does not trigger on a tie. When the effect requires giving up part of the damage, the attacker decides after winning and before calculating it.
Lethal — on winning an Attack, each pair of dice showing 10 on the attacker's roll adds the weapon's Damage once more to the damage dealt.
Sweep — on winning a melee Attack, the attacker can give up the Margin. The original target takes only the weapon's Damage, and a second target of the attacker's choice takes the same Damage as superficial damage. The second target must be within the weapon's reach and adjacent to the original target; they do not make another roll to respond.
Debilitating (Shaken) — on winning an Attack, the attacker can give up the weapon's Damage. The target takes only the Margin and becomes Shaken.
Debilitating (Slowed) — on winning an Attack, the attacker can give up the weapon's Damage. The target takes only the Margin and becomes Slowed.
Momentum — on winning an Attack, the attacker's next Attack against the same target, until the end of their next Turn, gets +1 die. Momentum bonuses do not stack.
Graze — when the target wins the Attack, they still take half the weapon's Damage, rounded up, as superficial damage. It does not apply if the attacker got no Successes.
Displace — on winning an Attack, the attacker can move the target 1 square in any direction, with no other roll, following the limits of Reposition.
Puncture — on winning an Attack, the target's Effective Absorption is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0.
Modules and settings can add new properties, origins, materials and weapons to the core catalog.
Mastering a Weapon
Mastering a weapon means knowing it well enough to draw out its Mastery.
When an Attack Skill (Fighting, Shooting or Throwing) reaches 5, the character masters one specific weapon of their choice that uses that Skill.
Each additional weapon costs 3 XP (see Advancement) and requires 5 in one of the Skills the weapon uses.
Mastery is of the weapon, not of the effect: mastering the Battle Axe does not grant the Mastery of another weapon with the same effect.
A character who masters a weapon uses its Mastery on any Attack made with it, whatever the Attack's Skill.
Unarmed Attacks have no Mastery.
Narrator characters master the weapons the Narrator chooses.
Damage Types
The Damage Type tells the nature of the wound — a piece of information separate from the damage's severity (see Damage Severity).
The starting list of damage types is:
Physical: Slashing, Bludgeoning, Piercing
Elemental: Fire, Ice, Electric, Acid, Poison
Magic: Magic
Each damage source defines its Damage Type — for example, a sword deals Slashing, a mace deals Bludgeoning and a fire spell deals Fire. Catalogs and modules can add new damage types.

regras/equipamentos/armaduras.text:
Armor is equipment used to protect the character.
The armor available in the core is in the Armor Catalog.
Each armor is described by the following fields:
Field Description 
Name the armor's name 
Category Light, Medium or Heavy (see Categories) 
Absorption how many points of aggravated damage are converted into superficial 
Minimum Strength the Strength needed to wear the armor without losing Movement 
Load how much of the Maximum Load it takes 
Value the armor's cost 
Properties the armor's special traits (see Properties) 
Absorption
An armor's Absorption tells how much aggravated damage taken is converted into superficial damage.
When taking damage from an Attack, the character converts to superficial a number of points of aggravated damage equal to their Absorption — never more than the aggravated damage taken. Total Absorption is the sum of the character's base Absorption and the Absorption of the armor worn. A character wears one armor at a time. Base Absorption can be raised or lowered by effects, but never goes below 0.
For example: an armor with Absorption 2 takes an Attack that deals 3 aggravated damage. 2 points are converted into superficial damage, and only 1 point stays aggravated.
Damage that is already superficial is not affected: armor only reduces how much damage stays aggravated.
Resistances and Vulnerabilities to specific Damage Types can raise or lower this absorption (see Resistance and Vulnerability).
Categories
Every armor has a Category, which organizes its Absorption, Dodge penalty, Minimum Strength and typical Load.
Category Absorption When Dodging Minimum Strength Load 
Light 1 no penalty — 1 
Medium 2 to 3 -2 to -3 dice 2 2 
Heavy 4 to 5 -4 to -5 dice 3 3 to 4 
Dodge: with Medium or Heavy armor, the Dodge Pool loses dice equal to the armor's Absorption. The character's base Absorption and Resistances do not count.
Minimum Strength: with Strength below the Minimum Strength of the armor worn, the character has -2 Movement.
Heavy: every Heavy armor is Noisy (see Properties).
Putting On and Taking Off
Putting on an armor takes 1 minute (Light), 5 minutes (Medium) or 10 minutes (Heavy). Taking it off takes 1 minute (Light or Medium) or 5 minutes (Heavy). An armor cannot be put on or taken off during a Tactical Scene.
Properties
Properties are an armor's special traits. The starting list of properties is:
[Type] Resistance (value) — the armor grants Resistance to the given Damage Type. The value is added to Effective Absorption against that Type — for example, an armor with Absorption 2 and Slashing Resistance 1 has Effective Absorption 3 against Slashing and 2 against the other Types.
[Type] Vulnerability (value) — the armor leaves the wearer vulnerable to the given Damage Type. The value is subtracted from Effective Absorption against that Type — for example, metal armors have Electric Vulnerability 1: a Chain Mail with Absorption 4 ends up with 3 against Electric.
Noisy — the armor imposes -2 dice on Stealth tests.
Modules and settings can add new properties and armors to the core catalog.

regras/equipamentos/escudos.text:
Shields are equipment used for defense.
The shields available in the core are in the Shield Catalog.
A character equipped with a Shield can choose to Defend in a Confront (see Confront).
Each shield is described by the following fields:
Field Description 
Name the shield's name 
Category Light, Medium or Heavy (see Categories) 
Protection bonus granted when Defending 
Minimum Strength the Strength needed to use the shield without losing Movement 
Load how much of the Maximum Load it takes 
Value the shield's cost 
Properties the shield's special traits (see Properties) 
Protection
When choosing to Defend, the character adds the shield's Protection to their Dice Pool (see Confront).
Categories
Category Protection Minimum Strength Load Other cost 
Light 2 — 1 — 
Medium 3 2 1 — 
Heavy 4 3 2 -1 die when Attacking 
With Strength below the Minimum Strength of the shield in hand, the character has -2 Movement (the same penalty as armor, which does not stack).
Properties

regras/equipamentos/consumiveis.text:
A Consumable is a piece of equipment that is spent in a single use. In the core, Consumables are Drugs and alchemicals (remedies, bombs, poisons and oils), gathered in the Consumable Catalog.
Using a Consumable
Drawing a Consumable follows the rules of Switching Equipment.
Using a Consumable on yourself or on an adjacent creature takes an Action. A creature that does not want the effect must be the target of a Confront.
A Consumable with Thrown is used with Confront, like a Thrown weapon (see Weapons). It is spent even if the Attack fails.
Applying to a weapon takes an Action. The effect applies to the next Attack that deals damage with it, until the end of the Scene.
The same Consumable does not stack on the same creature: using it again only renews the duration.
No Consumable recovers damage to Health or Willpower.
Drugs
Drugs are Consumables that strengthen the body or the mind at a price. A Drug lasts until the end of the Scene or, outside a Tactical Scene, for 1 hour. It has three parts:
Effect: what the Drug grants while it lasts.
Cost: the penalty the character suffers while the Drug lasts.
Conditions applied by a Drug, such as Numbed or Dazzled, last as long as the Drug.
Crash: when the Drug ends, the character pays the rest of the bill, equal to the Grade:
body Drugs give stacks of Impaired;
mind Drugs deal superficial Willpower damage.
A creature can be under only one Drug at a time. Using another ends the first, and its Crash happens at once.
Grades
Every Drug comes in five Grades. The Grade sets the strength of the Effect, the Costs, the Crash and the Value.
Grade Name Costs Value 
1 Diluted the Cost 25 
2 Common the Cost 50 
3 Concentrated the Cost and the extra Cost 150 
4 Strong the Cost and the extra Cost 400 
5 Pure the doubled Cost and the extra Cost 1000 
Effects
Each effect has an Intensity. The sum of a Drug's Intensities equals its Grade.
Effect Intensity 
+1 to an Attribute. The Attribute can go above 5, with no limit. The bonus applies to rolls and requirements, but does not change Health, Willpower, Load or Initiative 1 per point 
Resistance 1 to a Damage Type 1 per point 
+2 base Movement 1 per +2 
Ignore a Condition: Fear, Stunned, Poisoned, Slowed, Shaken or Challenged has no effect while the Drug lasts 1 each 
Darkvision up to 6 squares 1 
becomes Numbed: ignores the penalties of Debilitated, Impaired and Poisoned 2 
becomes Lucid: the next Willpower use costs no Willpower damage 2 
becomes Relentless: does not become Incapacitated while the Drug lasts 3 
Costs
Cost Effect Doubled 
Attribute -1 to an Attribute the Drug does not strengthen -2 
Vulnerability Vulnerability 1 to a Damage Type Vulnerability 2 
Heavy -2 base Movement -4 
Dazzled becomes Dazzled: Bright counts as Dim — 
Unsteady becomes Unsteady: at the end of each Turn, may lose their next Movement — 
Dazzled and Unsteady cannot be doubled, so they only appear as the extra Cost.

regras/equipamentos/trocar-equipamento.title: Switching Equipment
regras/equipamentos/trocar-equipamento.summary: During a Tactical Scene, the character can draw, stow and switch equipment.
regras/equipamentos/trocar-equipamento.text:
During a Tactical Scene, the character can draw, stow and switch equipment.
Drawing and Stowing
Once per Turn, the character can draw or stow one piece of equipment without spending an Action, as part of their Movement or Action. For example, they can draw their sword and start a Confront as part of the same Action.
Dropping a piece of equipment on the ground never takes an Action.
Switching Equipment
Doing more than that in the same Turn, such as stowing one weapon and drawing another, takes the Switching Equipment Action.
The switch can involve a single item or a set of equipment, as long as the change can reasonably be made during the Turn. For example, a character could use Switching Equipment to:
replace a sword with a bow;
stow a weapon and equip a shield;
swap a weapon and shield for a weapon that needs both hands;
replace the set of equipment currently in use with another prepared set.
The chosen equipment counts as in use as soon as the Action is complete.
Picking Up from the Ground
Picking up a piece of equipment from the ground takes the Switching Equipment Action, even with a free hand. This includes recovering a weapon lost to Disarm.
Armor cannot be put on or taken off during a Tactical Scene (see Putting On and Taking Off).

regras/resistencia-e-vulnerabilidade/res.summary: This section gathers the rules that define how characters and creatures react to damage from specific Damage Types and Materials, through Resistances, Vulnerabilities and Immunities. They can be granted by equipment…
regras/resistencia-e-vulnerabilidade/res.text:
This section gathers the rules that define how characters and creatures react to damage from specific Damage Types and Materials, through Resistances, Vulnerabilities and Immunities.
They can be granted by equipment, Conditions, origins, creatures, spells or effects.
Concepts
Resistance — a value that helps convert aggravated damage into superficial damage.
Vulnerability — a value that reduces absorption and increases the damage taken.
Immunity — no value; damage of the Type or Material simply does not apply.
Resistances, Vulnerabilities and Immunities to Materials are, for now, set directly on characters and creatures. Armor still grants Resistances only to Damage Types.
Effective Absorption
When taking damage, the Effective Absorption is calculated considering the Damage Type taken and the Material of the weapon that caused it, if any:
Effective Absorption = total Absorption (base Absorption + armor Absorption) + Σ Resistances to the Type and the Material - Σ Vulnerabilities to the Type and the Material
The values for the Type and the Material are added together. When the damage source has no Material, only the Damage Type is considered.
Effective Absorption greater than or equal to the aggravated damage: all the damage is converted into superficial damage.
Effective Absorption between 0 and the damage: only the part covered by the absorption is converted; the rest stays aggravated (see Armor).
Negative Effective Absorption: when the character takes at least 1 point of damage from that source, the negative value is added to the damage taken (as an absolute value) and all the damage is aggravated — no conversion is possible (see Vulnerability).
Damage that is already superficial is not affected by positive absorption.
Immunity to the Type or the Material takes precedence over everything: the damage is ignored before Effective Absorption is even calculated, even if there is Vulnerability to the other.
Examples
A character with Absorption 1 and Fire Resistance 3 takes 4 Fire damage: the Effective Absorption is 4, and the 4 points are converted into superficial damage.
A character with Fire Vulnerability 3 and Absorption 0 takes 1 Fire damage: the Effective Absorption is -3, and they take 4 aggravated Fire damage.
A character with Fire Immunity takes 4 Fire damage: the damage does not apply, and no damage is taken.
A character with Absorption 2 and Fire Vulnerability 3 takes 1 Fire damage: the Effective Absorption is -1, and they take 2 aggravated Fire damage.
A creature with Absorption 0, Slashing Resistance 3 and Silver Vulnerability 3 takes Slashing damage from a Silver weapon: the Effective Absorption is 0, since the values cancel out.
A creature with Common metal Immunity takes damage from an iron or steel weapon: no damage is taken, whatever the weapon's Damage Type. This Immunity does not apply to Silver or Meteorite weapons.
Relations
Damage Types and Materials are defined in Weapons. The severity of damage and its recovery are described in Health.
Damage dealt by Zones does not use Effective Absorption. In that case, Resistances and Vulnerabilities are added together as in Effective Absorption: a positive total converts that many points of the Zone's aggravated damage into superficial before applying the test's Successes, a negative total increases the Zone's Damage, and Immunities prevent the damage entirely.

For now, Resistances to Materials are set directly on characters and creatures; armor grants Resistances only to Damage Types.

When calculating Effective Absorption, Vulnerabilities to the weapon's Damage Type and Material are added together and subtracted from the absorption. That is why a Vulnerability eats into the armor's Absorption before it becomes extra damage.

the negative value is added to the damage taken (as an absolute value);
all the damage then becomes aggravated — no conversion is possible, even if the damage taken would originally have been superficial.
For example, a character with Absorption 2 and Fire Vulnerability 3 has Effective Absorption -1 against Fire; 1 Fire damage becomes 2 aggravated damage.

regras/condicoes/condicoes.title: Conditions
regras/condicoes/condicoes.summary: A Condition is a state that affects a character during a Scene, imposing mechanical effects while it stays active. Conditions are applied by Actions, Maneuvers, Capabilities or other rules. They are all gathered here as…
regras/condicoes/condicoes.text:
A Condition is a state that affects a character during a Scene, imposing mechanical effects while it stays active.
Conditions are applied by Actions, Maneuvers, Capabilities or other rules. They are all gathered here as the single core reference.
General rules
Duration: unless stated otherwise, a Condition ends at the end of the Scene. Conditions tied to the Health track and those with their own way of ending, such as Prone and Grappled, follow their own rules.
Turns: a duration in Turns counts the affected character's Turns. The Condition ends at the end of the last of those Turns. If it is applied during the affected character's Turn, that Turn does not count.
Applying again: a Condition the character already has does not stack. It only renews the duration, and the duration that ends last applies. Stacking Conditions, such as Fear, Aiming, Impaired and Bleeding, say how they stack.
Conditions
Prone — on the ground; penalizes their own rolls and changes Attacks made against them.
Grappled — held by another character; no movement.
Debilitated — Health track full.
Incapacitated — whole Health track aggravated; prone, unable to act or respond.
Slowed — reduced Movement until the next Turn of whoever applied it.
Shaken — penalty on the next Attack.
Poisoned — penalty on Physical rolls.
Paralyzed — no Action and no Movement.
Stunned — no Action.
Fear — stacking penalty on every Pool.
Bleeding — stacking superficial damage at the end of each Turn.
Patched — Health damage eased by a Patch Up until the end of the Scene, which comes back afterward.
Impaired — stacking penalty on Physical rolls after a Patch Up; removed by Treatment and Long Rest.
Numbed — ignores the penalties of Debilitated, Impaired and Poisoned.
Lucid — the next Willpower use costs no Willpower damage.
Relentless — does not become Incapacitated while it lasts.
Dazzled — Bright counts as Dim.
Unsteady — may lose Movement at the end of each Turn.
Aiming — stacks the bonus of the Aim Maneuver for the next ranged Attack.
Read — analyzed by another character; no effect of its own, used by Capabilities.
Challenged — provoked by a Duelist; penalizes Confronts started against other creatures.
Relations
Conditions are usually applied by Maneuvers and other effects during Scenes and Conflicts.

regras/condicoes/caido.title: Prone
regras/condicoes/caido.summary: A Prone character stays on the ground and their movement becomes Special Movement, done by crawling. Melee Attacks against a Prone character get: +2 dice on the Dice Pool. Ranged Attacks against a Prone character get…
regras/condicoes/caido.text:
A Prone character stays on the ground and their movement becomes Special Movement, done by crawling.
Melee Attacks against a Prone character get:
+2 dice on the Dice Pool
Ranged Attacks against a Prone character get:
-2 dice on the Dice Pool
A Prone character also gets:
-2 dice on their own Dice Pools
To stop being Prone, the character spends half of their base Movement, rounded up, from the Movement they still have on their own Turn. Standing up does not take an Action.
Without enough Movement, such as a character with Movement 0 or Grappled, they cannot stand up.

regras/condicoes/agarrado.title: Grappled
regras/condicoes/agarrado.summary: A Grappled character suffers the following effects. Movement 0. When making an Attack against any target other than the character grappling them, the Grappled character gets: -2 dice on the Dice Pool. Attacks made…
regras/condicoes/agarrado.text:
A Grappled character suffers the following effects.
Movement 0
When making an Attack against any target other than the character grappling them, the Grappled character gets:
-2 dice on the Dice Pool
Attacks made against whoever is holding the grapple do not suffer this penalty.
Grappling takes a free hand, which stays occupied while the grapple lasts. Creatures without hands grapple with the body part their sheet sets.
Dragging
Whoever holds the grapple can drag the target while moving, as long as the target is at most one Size category larger. This movement is Special Movement for the grappler. On each square, the grappler places the target in a square adjacent to them. For the target, this is forced movement.
End of the grapple
The grappler can release the target at any moment, without using their Action. The grapple also ends when the two stop being adjacent or when the grappler becomes Incapacitated or Paralyzed.
When the Condition comes from an effect with no character grappling, such as the Web, the release and adjacency rules do not apply, and the effect sets how to escape.
How to escape
During their Turn, a Grappled character can use their Action to try to escape.
To do so, they make a new opposed roll against the character holding the grapple:
Grappled character: Strength + Athletics or Agility + Acrobatics, at their choice
Character holding the grapple: Strength + Athletics
Capabilities and other rules can replace these Pools. The way the attempt is described does not allow freely swapping the Attribute or the Skill.
If the Grappled character gets more Successes, the Grappled Condition ends. On a tie or a win for the character holding the grapple, the condition remains.

The Condition ends when at least 1 point of aggravated Health damage is converted into superficial, usually through Treatment.
The fate of an Incapacitated character who keeps taking damage is up to the Narrator.

regras/condicoes/remendado.summary: A Patched creature has received a Patch Up and has a number of eased points. Until the end of the Scene, each eased point changes its Health damage: one point of aggravated damage becomes superficial; if it has no…
regras/condicoes/remendado.text:
A Patched creature has received a Patch Up and has a number of eased points. Until the end of the Scene, each eased point changes its Health damage:
one point of aggravated damage becomes superficial;
if it has no aggravated damage, one point of superficial damage is erased.
Note how many points were converted and how many were erased. An Incapacitated creature that is Patched stops being Incapacitated, because its track now has superficial damage.
End of the Scene
At the end of the Scene, the eased damage comes back:
the creature takes superficial damage equal to the erased points;
then, a number of points of superficial damage equal to the converted points becomes aggravated.
This follows the Full Health Track rules and can leave the creature Incapacitated, but this damage never kills it.
Then the Condition ends and the creature becomes Impaired, with 1 stack for each eased point.

-1 die on rolls that use a Physical Attribute
The penalty adds to that of Debilitated, when the Health track is full.
The Condition does not end at the end of the Scene. Each Treatment received removes 1 stack, in addition to its normal effect, and each completed Long Rest removes 1 stack.
Becoming Impaired again adds the stacks to those the character already has.
Impaired is applied by the end of the Patched Condition and can be applied by other Capabilities or effects that refer to this Condition.

regras/condicoes/anestesiado.html:
A Numbed character feels no pain. They ignore the dice penalties of:

  • Debilitated;
  • Impaired;
  • Poisoned.

The Condition lasts as long as its source says. It does not remove those Conditions: when Numbed ends, the penalties apply again.

Numbed can be applied by Drugs, Capabilities or other effects that refer to this Condition.

regras/condicoes/obstinado.summary: A Relentless character refuses to fall. While the Condition lasts, they do not become Incapacitated, even with their whole Health track filled with aggravated damage. They are still Debilitated with a full track. When…

regras/condicoes/mirando.summary: An Aiming character has used the Aim Maneuver and is focusing before attacking. Each stack gives: +2 dice on the next ranged Attack, against any target. The benefit applies whether the Attack uses Shooting, Throwing or…
regras/condicoes/mirando.text:
An Aiming character has used the Aim Maneuver and is focusing before attacking. Each stack gives:
+2 dice on the next ranged Attack, against any target
The benefit applies whether the Attack uses Shooting, Throwing or another Attribute set by a rule.
The character holds at most a number of stacks equal to their Cunning.
All stacks are lost if, before attacking, the character:
uses their Movement while Aiming;
is moved by force;
takes damage;
becomes Prone.
The stacks do not apply to responses to a Confront.
Making the Attack also ends the Aim, unless a Capability expressly says otherwise.
The Condition also ends at the end of the Scene.

regras/condicoes/lido.summary: A Read character has been analyzed by another character, who now understands their emotions, intentions, strengths and weaknesses. The Condition always belongs to whoever applied it. A character can be Read by one…
regras/condicoes/lido.text:
A Read character has been analyzed by another character, who now understands their emotions, intentions, strengths and weaknesses.
The Condition always belongs to whoever applied it. A character can be Read by one opponent and not by the others.
Read imposes no effect by itself. The Capabilities that refer to this Condition determine the benefits of whoever applied it against the Read character.
The Condition ends at the end of the Scene.
Read is applied, for example, by the Mentalist's Cold Read and the Hunter's Know the Prey.

regras/condicoes/desafiado.summary: A Challenged character was provoked by a Duelist to remain in combat against them. The Condition belongs to the Duelist who applied it. The Challenged character takes -3 dice when starting a Confront against any other…

regras/competencias/competencias.title: Competencies
regras/competencias/competencias.summary: Competencies represent developed ways of acting, fighting, thinking or interacting with the world. Each has its own identity and a fixed progression. A character can develop several Competencies and combine their…
regras/competencias/competencias.text:
Competencies represent developed ways of acting, fighting, thinking or interacting with the world. Each has its own identity and a fixed progression.
A character can develop several Competencies and combine their progressions freely.
Level
Every Competency has a Level from 0 to 5, unless its progression sets a lower maximum Level.
Level 0: the character does not have the Competency;
Levels 1 to 5: the character has every Capability granted up to that Level.
Each increase automatically grants the content set for the new Level, with no choices from a catalog and no separate purchase for the Capability. To reach a Level, the character must have every previous Level of the same Competency.
Capabilities
Capabilities are the mechanical effects granted by a Competency's Levels. They can change any part of the system when their description says so, including Pools, Successes, Actions, Maneuvers, damage, movement, range, resources, traits and formulas.
A Capability can also replace an Attribute, a Skill or another rule. When there is a conflict, the Capability's more specific rule takes precedence within the context it describes.
Choices can be part of how a Capability works, but they do not change the Competency's fixed progression.
More than one Competency
The character can have Levels in several Competencies.
Focusing Levels on a single Competency rewards specialization and brings the character closer to its Level 5. Spreading Levels across Competencies broadens their versatility and lets them combine different styles.
Total Competency Level
The Total Competency Level is the sum of the Levels the character has in all their Competencies.
Total Competency Level = sum of the Levels of every Competency.
This value is not a global character Level. It exists to set the cost of acquiring new Competency Levels.
Character creation
At creation, the character receives 2 Competency Points (see Character Creation).
Acquiring during the campaign
To acquire any new Competency Level, the character pays a cost based on the new Total Competency Level:
XP cost = new Total Competency Level × 3.
After paying, the character raises by 1 the Level of a Competency they already have or acquires Level 1 of a new Competency. The new Level's content is received automatically and needs no further XP.
Current Total Level New Total Level Cost 
2 3 9 XP 
3 4 12 XP 
4 5 15 XP 
5 6 18 XP 
6 7 21 XP 
There is no limit to the Total Competency Level. The steadily rising XP cost naturally limits how many Levels are accumulated.
Format of a Competency
Each Competency presents its identity, a Progression table and a section for each Level, with the name and effect of the Capabilities it grants. A Level can grant a new Capability or increase the potency of one the character already has.
List of Competencies
Acrobat — Dodges that carry you farther and through enemies, greater Movement, resisting being surrounded, escaping Zones and winning ties when Dodging.
Ambidextrous — fighting with a weapon in each hand, adding the off-hand weapon's Damage as dice when Attacking, Dodging and Parrying, and at Level 3 any one-handed weapon as the off-hand weapon.
Parrier — Parrying Attacks with your own weapon, adding its Damage when Defending, first in melee and then at range as well.
Assassin — acting first in Initiative, surprising, extra damage against targets without a response, Stealth and a quick arrival in combat.
Marksman — shooting stance with a bonus and longer range, free Aim every Turn, moving without losing the Aim and Aim stacks paid with Willpower.
Hunter — tracking with Survival, studying any non-Humanoid creature with Nature or Occultism, stronger Attacks and damage against Read prey and a hunt that is never lost.
Captivating — appearance that favors social interactions and makes a stronger first impression.
Duelist — fighting with a weapon in one hand and the other free, an edge against isolated targets, resistance to being surrounded and challenges that bind the opponent to you.
Furious — Fury, melee aggression, damage that grows with wounds, a fast advance, immunity to Fear and refusing to fall.
Guardian — Defending with a Shield for yourself and your allies: Cover Ally on Defend and Dodge, swapping places to take an Attack, Protection against Zones and blocking on a tie.
Inspirer — Helping allies at range with a bigger bonus, transferring Willpower and inspiring several allies at once.
Mentalist — reading people and enemies through the Read Condition, Cunning on Attacks, Perception and social tests, and guaranteed dice against those you have read.
Robust — a larger Health track that grows with the Competency's Level.
Sentinel — Opportunity Attacks against anyone who leaves your melee weapon's reach or attacks your allies, stopping the target's movement.
Medic — Patch Up that keeps a wounded ally fighting until the end of the Scene, ignoring Debilitated, more efficient Treatment without supplies, and Proper Facilities Treatment anywhere.
All Capabilities, with the rules for their use by NPCs, are gathered in Capabilities.

regras/competencias/acrobata.title: Acrobat
regras/competencias/acrobata.summary: Acrobat represents the character who slips past blows, crosses the battlefield and refuses to be surrounded.
regras/competencias/acrobata.text:
Acrobat represents the character who slips past blows, crosses the battlefield and refuses to be surrounded.
Progression
Level Capability granted Light Feet 
1 Acrobatic Dodge — 
2 Light Feet +2 
3 Hard to Surround +3 
4 Evasion +4 
5 Untouchable +5 
Level 1 — Acrobatic Dodge
When you win a Dodge, you can move up to your full base Movement, instead of half of it.
During this movement, you can pass through squares occupied by enemies, but you cannot end it in one of them.
Level 2 — Light Feet
Your base Movement increases by a number of squares equal to your Acrobat Level. The increase also applies to Run and to the movement when Dodging.
In addition:
Difficult Terrain costs only 1 Movement point per square for you. Special Movement still costs 2 points;
standing up from Prone costs only 1 Movement point. With Movement 0, you still cannot stand up.
Level 3 — Hard to Surround
Attackers do not get Numerical Advantage against you. You still count as usual toward your allies' Numerical Advantage.
During your Movement, you can pass through squares occupied by enemies. Each one costs 1 extra Movement point, and you cannot end your movement in one of them.
These effects do not work while you are unable to move.
Level 4 — Evasion
When resisting a Damage Zone, if you get Successes equal to or greater than the Zone's Damage and can leave the area with the movement of a won Dodge, you move out of the Zone and take no damage. This movement is a Dodge's movement and follows its rules. It must end outside the Zone's area.
If you do not get enough Successes, cannot leave the area or choose not to move, resisting the Zone is resolved as usual.
Level 5 — Untouchable
When Dodging, you win on a tie: you avoid all damage and can make the Acrobatic Dodge movement.

regras/competencias/ambidestro.title: Ambidextrous
regras/competencias/ambidestro.summary: Ambidextrous represents the fighter who uses both weapons in the same strike: while one opens the enemy's guard, the other lands the blow. The Capabilities of this Competency require a melee weapon held in each hand…
regras/competencias/ambidestro.text:
Ambidextrous represents the fighter who uses both weapons in the same strike: while one opens the enemy's guard, the other lands the blow.
The Capabilities of this Competency require a melee weapon held in each hand, following Two-Weapon Fighting. The off-hand weapon must have the Light Property. When attacking or Accepting the Confront, it must also be able to reach the opponent in the Confront.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Double Strike 
2 Cross Guard 
3 Ambidexterity 
Level 1 — Double Strike
When you start a Confront with a melee Attack or Accept the Confront with a melee weapon, you add to the Pool a number of dice equal to the off-hand weapon's Damage:
Pool = the main weapon's Attack Pool + off-hand weapon Damage
The damage dealt is still the main weapon's.
Level 2 — Cross Guard
When you Dodge or Parry a melee Attack, you also add the off-hand weapon's Damage to the Pool as dice.
When Parrying, the main weapon is the one used to Parry and adds its own Damage normally.
Level 3 — Ambidexterity
The off-hand weapon can be any one-handed melee weapon, not only a Light weapon. A Flexible weapon counts as a one-handed weapon and uses its one-handed Damage.

regras/competencias/aparador.title: Parrier
regras/competencias/aparador.summary: Parrier represents the character trained to block blows with their own weapon, without relying on a shield.
regras/competencias/aparador.text:
Parrier represents the character trained to block blows with their own weapon, without relying on a shield.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Parry 
2 Parry Projectiles 
Level 1 — Parry
You can Parry: choose to Defend against a melee Attack using a melee weapon you are holding, even without a Shield.
When Parrying, instead of the normal Defend Pool, you use the same Pool as a melee Attack with the weapon used and, in place of the Shield's Protection, add the weapon's Damage:
Parry Pool = the weapon's Attack Pool + weapon Damage
Rules that change the weapon's Attack Pool, such as Heavy or a Capability, also apply to Parrying.
Bonuses and penalties that depend on starting an Attack, such as Numerical Advantage, do not apply to Parrying.
The Damage counted includes the +1 of a Flexible weapon held in both hands. The weapon's Mastery is not triggered when Parrying. The rest follows the normal Defend rules.
If you are fighting with two weapons, you choose which of them you use to Parry. The Damage of the two weapons is not added together, except through the Ambidextrous Cross Guard.
If you are also equipped with a Shield, you choose when Defending whether to use the Shield's Protection or the weapon's Damage. The two bonuses do not stack.
Unarmed and other Natural weapons cannot be used to Parry, unless another Capability allows it.
Level 2 — Parry Projectiles
You can also Parry ranged Attacks, including shots and thrown weapons, still using a melee weapon.

Bonuses and penalties that depend on starting an Attack, such as Numerical Advantage, do not apply to Parrying.

regras/competencias/assassino.title: Assassin
regras/competencias/assassino.summary: Assassin represents the character who reaches the target unnoticed, acts first and strikes before the opponent can react.
regras/competencias/assassino.text:
Assassin represents the character who reaches the target unnoticed, acts first and strikes before the opponent can react.
Progression

1 First Strike — — 
2 Sneak Attack +2 — 
3 Silent Steps +3 +3 dice 
4 Lethal Approach +4 +4 dice

Level 1 — First Strike
Your Initiative Pool can use Agility instead of Determination:
Initiative Pool = Cunning + Agility
If the Tactical Scene begins without the enemies having noticed your presence, you also add to your Initiative Pool a number of dice equal to your Stealth Level. The Narrator decides whether the enemies had already noticed you.
When you start a Confront against a target whose first Turn in the Scene has not yet come, the target is considered surprised and becomes a target without a response.
A target who used Delay the Turn is not considered surprised. A participant who joins the Scene after it begins is considered surprised until their first Turn comes.
Level 2 — Sneak Attack
When you win an Attack against a target without a response, you add to the damage an amount equal to your Assassin Level.
The bonus applies whatever the reason the target cannot respond, including when they were surprised by First Strike. It also applies outside a Tactical Scene, when the Narrator determines that the target does not notice the Attack.
The bonus adds to the weapon's Damage, applies to any kind of Attack and does not add dice to the Pool. It does not apply on a tie.
Level 3 — Silent Steps
You get a number of extra dice equal to your Assassin Level on every Stealth and Sleight of Hand test.
This bonus does not apply to the Initiative Pool, nor to the Stealth Level added by First Strike.
Level 4 — Lethal Approach
On your first Turn of each Tactical Scene, you get the effect of the Run Action without spending your Action.

regras/competencias/atirador.title: Marksman
regras/competencias/atirador.summary: Marksman represents the character who prepares their shots and keeps their Aim to hit a target with precision. Its Capabilities apply to any Attack with the Shooting Skill.
regras/competencias/atirador.text:
Marksman represents the character who prepares their shots and keeps their Aim to hit a target with precision. Its Capabilities apply to any Attack with the Shooting Skill.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Shooting Stance 
2 Unshakable Focus 
3 Steady Aim 
4 Improved Shooting Stance 
5 Unwavering Focus 
Level 1 — Shooting Stance
You can take a Shooting Stance before making an Attack with Shooting, if you have not moved yet this Turn. It lasts until the end of the Turn and, while in it:
you get +2 dice to the Pool of Attacks made with Shooting;
you ignore the first -2 dice penalty for attacking beyond the weapon's normal range;
you cannot move until the end of the Turn.
Level 2 — Unshakable Focus
At the start of your Turn, if you have no Aiming stacks, you get 1 Aiming stack without spending your Action.
In addition, being forcibly moved does not make you lose your Aiming stacks. You still lose them if you take damage or another usual condition for losing the Aim happens.
Level 3 — Steady Aim
You can take the Shooting Stance even after moving and, while in it, you can move. The total in the Turn cannot exceed half your base Movement.
This move does not make you lose your Aiming stacks.
Level 4 — Improved Shooting Stance
While in the Shooting Stance, you can take any amount of superficial Willpower damage. For each point taken, you get 1 Aiming stack without spending your Action. The stack limit set by your Cunning still applies, and points taken beyond that limit grant no stacks.
Level 5 — Unwavering Focus
Your Unshakable Focus evolves. At the start of your Turn, you get 1 Aiming stack without spending your Action, even if you already have stacks.
In addition, the maximum number of Aiming stacks you can have becomes:
Cunning + 5
This limit replaces the one set by Cunning in every rule, including Improved Shooting Stance.

regras/competencias/cacador.title: Hunter
regras/competencias/cacador.summary: Hunter represents the character who lives off the wilds and the creatures that dwell in them. They follow tracks others cannot see, know the animals, monsters and supernatural creatures they pursue in depth and use that…
regras/competencias/cacador.text:
Hunter represents the character who lives off the wilds and the creatures that dwell in them. They follow tracks others cannot see, know the animals, monsters and supernatural creatures they pursue in depth and use that knowledge to bring them down.
This Competency's Capabilities use the Survival Skill, the Nature Specific Knowledge: in-depth knowledge of the fauna, flora, terrain and climate of the wilds; and the Occultism Skill.
A prey is a creature of any Type except Humanoid. Against Beast, Plant, Monstrosity and Dragon, the study uses Nature; against Undead, Construct, Elemental, Spirit and Aberration, it uses Occultism.
Progression
Level Capability granted Weak Spot 
1 Tracker — 
2 Know the Prey — 
3 Hunter's Strike — 
4 Weak Spot +4 
5 Relentless Hunt +5 
Level 1 — Tracker
You get +2 dice on Survival tests to follow tracks and to erase your group's tracks.
When you successfully follow tracks, you also learn which creature left them, how many there are, how long ago they passed and whether they were wounded or in a hurry.
Level 2 — Know the Prey
You can use your Action to study a prey you can observe. Test Cunning + Nature or Cunning + Occultism, depending on the prey's Type, against a Difficulty set by the Narrator.
Whatever the result, the prey becomes Read by you until the end of the Scene. You cannot study a prey already Read by you.
Success: you ask the Narrator 1 question from the list below, plus 1 for each Success above the Difficulty.
Failure: you find out nothing.
Questions:
What is one of its Resistances or Immunities?
What is one of its Vulnerabilities?
What is one of its Capabilities?
How does it hunt, attack or defend itself?
Is it wounded, hungry or cornered?
Each question reveals a single Resistance, Immunity, Vulnerability or Capability. You can repeat a question to discover another. When the prey has none, the Narrator says so.
When following a prey's tracks with Tracker, you can make this test from the tracks, without spending an Action. The prey becomes Read by you during the first Scene in which you find it.
Level 3 — Hunter's Strike
You get +2 dice when starting a Confrontation with an Attack against a prey Read by you.
Level 4 — Weak Spot
When you attack a prey Read by you with a Damage Type or Material to which it has a Vulnerability, the weapon's Damage increases by an amount equal to your Hunter Level: +4 at Level 4 and +5 at Level 5.
The bonus applies to any kind of Attack, including on a tie, when the weapon's Damage is dealt as superficial damage. It does not add dice to the Pool.
Level 5 — Relentless Hunt
When you study a prey, you can mark it as your hunt. It remains Read by you across Scenes until it dies or you mark another. You can only have one hunt at a time.
You always know in which direction your hunt is, as long as it is in the wilds and within a day's travel of you.

regras/competencias/cativante.title: Captivating
regras/competencias/cativante.summary: Captivating represents a character whose beauty, elegance or personal presence influences how others perceive them.
regras/competencias/cativante.text:
Captivating represents a character whose beauty, elegance or personal presence influences how others perceive them.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Beautiful 
2 First Impression 
Level 1 — Beautiful
You gain +2 dice on social tests that use Charisma when your appearance can favor what you are trying to achieve.
The bonus can apply, for example, to Persuasion, Deception, Performance or Intimidation, depending on the approach used. It does not apply when the target cannot perceive you, when your appearance is irrelevant to the interaction or when it works against the desired result.
Level 2 — First Impression
The first time in each Scene that you make a test against a person that benefits from Beautiful, whatever the Skill or approach, the bonus increases from +2 to +4 dice.
