regras/competencias/duelista.title: Duelist
regras/competencias/duelista.summary: Duelist represents a fighter who uses a weapon in one hand and keeps the other free, facing opponents in individual combat. You are in a duel when only you and the target are adjacent to each other, with no other…
regras/competencias/duelista.text:
Duelist represents a fighter who uses a weapon in one hand and keeps the other free, facing opponents in individual combat.
You are in a duel when only you and the target are adjacent to each other, with no other combatants adjacent to either of you.
Duelist Capabilities only work while you hold a melee weapon in one hand and keep the other hand free.
Progression
Level Capability granted Singular Combat Technical Superiority Challenge 
1 Singular Combat +1 die — — 
2 Technical Superiority +2 dice −2 dice — 
3 Challenge +3 dice −3 dice −3 dice 
Level 1 — Singular Combat
You gain a number of extra dice equal to your Duelist Level when starting a melee Confront against a target with whom you are in a duel.
Level 2 — Technical Superiority
Reduce the Numerical Advantage bonus received on Attacks against you by an amount equal to your Duelist Level.
This reduction cannot make the bonus negative.
Level 3 — Challenge
You can use your Action to Challenge a creature that can perceive you.
Choose Intimidation, Deception or Persuasion and test Charisma + the chosen Skill against the target's Determination + Cunning.
If you win, the target becomes Challenged by you until the end of the Scene.
A Challenged creature takes -3 dice when starting a Confront against any creature other than you.
The Condition ends if you start a Confront against another creature.

regras/competencias/furioso.title: Furious
regras/competencias/furioso.summary: Furious represents the fighter who trades defense for aggression and turns pain and Willpower into brute force. Fury is a state of this Competency, not a Condition.
regras/competencias/furioso.text:
Furious represents the fighter who trades defense for aggression and turns pain and Willpower into brute force.
Fury is a state of this Competency, not a Condition.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Fury 
2 Blood for Blood 
3 Furious Charge 
4 Beyond Pain 
5 Refuse to Fall 
Level 1 — Fury
During a Tactical Scene, on your Turn, you can take 1 point of superficial Willpower damage to enter Fury. Entering Fury does not spend your Action.
Fury lasts until the end of your next Turn. Whenever you start a Confront with a melee Attack or a thrown weapon, the duration is extended until the end of your following Turn. Accepting the Confront does not extend Fury. It also ends at the end of the Scene.
While in Fury:
you can use Strength instead of the Attribute normally set for melee Attacks;
you get +2 dice to the Pool when starting a melee Confront;
you suffer −2 dice to the Pool when Defending and Dodging. Accepting the Confront does not suffer this penalty.
Level 2 — Blood for Blood
While in Fury, your melee Attacks get a bonus to weapon damage according to the damage marked on your Health track:
+1 for each point of superficial damage;
+2 for each point of aggravated damage.
The bonus is calculated when the Attack's damage is applied and is added to the weapon's damage bonus in every situation in which it is dealt, including on a tie, when the damage is dealt as superficial damage.
This bonus adds no dice to the Pool and does not apply to the counterattack when Accepting the Confront.
Level 3 — Furious Charge
While in Fury, your base Movement increases by +2 squares.
In addition, on entering Fury, you immediately get the effect of the Run Action on that Turn, without spending your Action.
Level 4 — Beyond Pain
While in Fury:
you ignore the Debilitated penalty;
you do not receive Fear stacks. On entering Fury, you lose every Fear stack you have.
Stacks lost on entering Fury do not come back when it ends.
Level 5 — Refuse to Fall
While in Fury, having your whole Health track filled with aggravated damage does not leave you Incapacitated. You keep acting as usual, but at the start of each of your Turns in this situation you must take 1 point of aggravated Willpower damage to stay on your feet.
In addition, each instance of Health damage you take in this situation, from any source, causes 1 point of aggravated Willpower damage, whatever the amount of damage dealt.
You become Incapacitated when:
you decide not to take the Willpower damage at the start of your Turn;
your whole Willpower track is filled with aggravated damage;
Fury ends, including at the end of the Scene.

regras/competencias/guardiao.title: Guardian
regras/competencias/guardiao.summary: Guardian represents the shield fighter who plants themselves between danger and those at their side, protecting themselves and extending their defense to their allies. The Capabilities of this Competency require you to…
regras/competencias/guardiao.text:
Guardian represents the shield fighter who plants themselves between danger and those at their side, protecting themselves and extending their defense to their allies.
The Capabilities of this Competency require you to be holding a Shield and use only its Protection. They do not apply without a Shield in hand, nor to Parry.
You cannot use Cover Ally or Intercept while you are surprised, Incapacitated or Paralyzed.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Cover Ally 
2 Shield Mastery 
3 Intercept 
4 Shelter 
5 Bulwark 
Level 1 — Cover Ally
Once per Round, when an ally adjacent to you is the target of an Attack, they add your Shield's Protection to their own Pool if they choose to Defend or Dodge. They can Defend even without a Shield:
Defend = the ally's Strength + Fighting + your Shield's Protection
Dodge = the ally's Agility + Acrobatics + your Shield's Protection
If the ally Defends holding a Shield of their own, they use the higher Protection of the two. The Protections do not stack.
You decide to use Cover Ally after the Attack is declared and before the ally chooses their response. If they Accept the Confront, the use for the Round is lost.
Level 2 — Shield Mastery
Shields you hold have their Minimum Strength reduced by 1 and do not impose the Heavy Shield's -1 die when Attacking penalty.
Level 3 — Intercept
When an ally adjacent to you is the target of an Attack, before they choose their response, you can take 1 point of superficial Willpower damage to swap places with them and become the target of the Attack.
You must respond to the Confront by Defending. The Attack keeps the Pool the attacker has already built.
Swapping places does not spend Movement and does not trigger effects caused by movement. If either of you does not fit in the other's space, you cannot Intercept.
In addition, Cover Ally improves: after the first use in a Round, you can use it again by taking 1 point of superficial Willpower damage for each additional use.
Level 4 — Shelter
When resisting a damage Zone, you can add your Shield's Protection to your own test Pool or to the Pool of an adjacent ally resisting the same Zone. The Protection applies to only one of these Pools.
If the chosen ally is holding a Shield, they use the higher Protection of the two. The Protections do not stack.
Level 5 — Bulwark
When Defending using your Shield's Protection, you win on a tie: the Attack is blocked and no one takes damage.
This also applies to the ally who Defends through Cover Ally.

This also applies to the ally who Defends through Cover Ally.

regras/competencias/inspirador.title: Inspirer
regras/competencias/inspirador.summary: Inspirer represents a character capable of awakening courage and determination through music, speeches, stories, performance or another form of expression.
regras/competencias/inspirador.text:
Inspirer represents a character capable of awakening courage and determination through music, speeches, stories, performance or another form of expression.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Inspiration 
2 Lift the Spirit 
3 Inspiring Chorus 
Level 1 — Inspiration
When you Help, the granted bonus increases from +1 to +2 dice.
You can Help a creature up to 6 squares away instead of needing to be adjacent, provided it can perceive you.
Level 2 — Lift the Spirit
Once per Scene, when you Help a creature through Inspiration, you can take 1 point of superficial Willpower damage to make it recover 1 point of superficial Willpower damage.
Level 3 — Inspiring Chorus
When you Help through Inspiration, you can take 1 point of superficial Willpower damage to choose a number of allies equal to your Charisma.
Each chosen ally must be within 6 squares and able to perceive you. They all gain the +2 dice from Inspiration on the next test they make before the end of their next Turn.
If you use Lift the Spirit, you take that Capability's cost separately and choose one of the allies to recover Willpower.

regras/competencias/mentalista.title: Mentalist
regras/competencias/mentalista.summary: Mentalist represents the character who reads people through trained observation, picking up emotions, intentions, lies and an enemy's strengths and weaknesses.
regras/competencias/mentalista.text:
Mentalist represents the character who reads people through trained observation, picking up emotions, intentions, lies and an enemy's strengths and weaknesses.
Progression
Level Capability granted Nothing Escapes 
1 Cold Read — 
2 Combat Read — 
3 Nothing Escapes +3 dice 
4 Manipulation +4 dice 
5 I Knew It +5 dice 
Level 1 — Cold Read
You can use your Action to analyze a person or creature you can observe. Test Cunning + Perception against the target's Charisma + Deception. A target who does not try to hide what they feel or does not know they are being observed is treated as a target without a response and counts as 1 Success.
Whatever the result, the target becomes Read by you until the end of the Scene. You cannot analyze a target already Read by you.
Win: you ask the Narrator a number of questions from the list below equal to your Margin of Successes.
Tie: you ask 1 question, but the target notices they are being analyzed.
Loss: you find out nothing, and the target notices they are being analyzed.
Questions about the person:
What are they feeling right now?
What do they want at this moment?
Are they hiding something? (yes or no)
What or whom are they afraid of?
What is one true fact about their life, such as their trade, their origin or a close relationship?
Questions about strengths and weaknesses:
What is one of their Resistances or Immunities?
What is one of their Vulnerabilities?
Each question about strengths and weaknesses reveals a single Resistance, Immunity or Vulnerability, with its Damage Type or Material. You can repeat a question to discover another. When the target has none, the Narrator says so.
The Narrator answers truthfully, the way the target's body and behavior reveal it: impressions, not exact thoughts, names or specific secrets. When the target is a player character, their player answers.
Level 2 — Combat Read
When starting a Confront or Accepting the Confront against a target Read by you, you can use Cunning instead of the Attribute normally set for the Attack's Pool.
The replacement applies to any kind of Attack and takes precedence over the Heavy property.
Level 3 — Nothing Escapes
You get a number of extra dice equal to your Mentalist Level on every Cunning + Perception test, including Cold Read.
Level 4 — Manipulation
On Persuasion, Intimidation and Deception tests, you get a number of extra dice equal to your Cunning.
These dice are a bonus, not a second Attribute: the test still uses the Skill's normal Attribute.
Level 5 — I Knew It
Before rolling any test whose Pool uses Cunning against a target Read by you, you can take up to 5 points of superficial Willpower damage. This includes Attacks made with Combat Read.
For each point taken, 1 die of that test's Pool becomes a guaranteed die: it is not rolled and counts as 1 Success.

regras/competencias/robusto.summary: Robust represents the character whose body withstands more wounds than usual, whether through natural constitution, training or a life of hardship.
regras/competencias/robusto.text:
Robust represents the character whose body withstands more wounds than usual, whether through natural constitution, training or a life of hardship.

2 +2 
3 +3

regras/competencias/sentinela.title: Sentinel
regras/competencias/sentinela.summary: Sentinel represents the fighter who controls the space around them, punishing anyone who tries to escape their weapon's reach and anyone who attacks their allies. The Capabilities of this Competency require you to be…
regras/competencias/sentinela.text:
Sentinel represents the fighter who controls the space around them, punishing anyone who tries to escape their weapon's reach and anyone who attacks their allies.
The Capabilities of this Competency require you to be holding a melee weapon and use its Reach. They do not work while you are surprised, Incapacitated or Paralyzed.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Opportunity Attack 
2 Halt 
3 Retaliate 
4 Tireless Vigilance 
Level 1 — Opportunity Attack
Once per Round, when an enemy creature within your melee weapon's Reach voluntarily moves out of it, you can start a Confront against it with that weapon, without spending your Action. The Attack happens before it leaves the Reach. Once it is resolved, the creature continues its Turn normally, if it can.
The target can only respond by Defending, which includes Parry, or Dodging. It cannot Accept the Confront.
Forced movement, such as from a Maneuver, and the movement of a won Dodge do not provoke an Opportunity Attack.
Level 2 — Halt
When you win an Opportunity Attack other than on a tie, the target's remaining Movement for that Turn becomes 0. It cannot move any more that Turn, not even by Running, but it can still use its Action in other ways.
On a tie, the Attack deals the normal tie damage and the target continues moving.
Level 3 — Retaliate
An Opportunity Attack can also be provoked when an enemy creature within your melee weapon's Reach starts a Confront against one of your allies. You attack after that Confront is resolved.
This use follows the same rules and the same per-Round limit, and Halt also applies to it.
Level 4 — Tireless Vigilance
After the first Opportunity Attack in a Round, you can make more by taking 1 point of superficial Willpower damage for each additional use.
Each movement or Confront provokes at most one Opportunity Attack from you.

regras/competencias/socorrista.title: Medic
regras/competencias/socorrista.summary: Medic represents the character who keeps the wounded on their feet during the fight, with patches made in the heat of combat, and cares for them more efficiently once it is over.
regras/competencias/socorrista.text:
Medic represents the character who keeps the wounded on their feet during the fight, with patches made in the heat of combat, and cares for them more efficiently once it is over.
Progression
Level Capability granted 
1 Patch Up 
2 Hold Fast 
3 Trained Hands 
4 Expert Patch 
5 Field Hospital 
Level 1 — Patch Up
In a Tactical Scene, you can use your Action to patch up an adjacent creature or yourself, spending 1 use of healing supplies, such as a Healing Kit. Roll Cunning + Healing and choose how many Successes to use, from 0 up to the total rolled.
The creature becomes Patched, with a number of eased points equal to the chosen Successes. At the end of the Scene, the eased damage comes back and it becomes Impaired.
Each creature can be Patched once per Scene.
Level 2 — Hold Fast
While Patched by you, the creature ignores the Debilitated penalty.
Level 3 — Trained Hands
Outside a Tactical Scene, when a Treatment you perform has at least 1 Success, it converts 1 more point of aggravated damage into superficial.
You treat and Patch Up without healing supplies, improvising with whatever is at hand.
Level 4 — Expert Patch
When a creature you Patched becomes Impaired at the end of the Scene, it receives half the stacks, rounded down.
Level 5 — Field Hospital
Outside a Tactical Scene, your Treatments count as performed in Proper Facilities.

regras/capacidades/capacidades.text:
Capabilities are the effects that Competencies grant at each Level. This page gathers all of them in a single list, together with the NPC Capabilities, which only NPCs have access to. The text of each one stays on its source page.
Player characters receive Capabilities only through the Levels of their Competencies. NPCs use the same sheet, simplified, but instead of Competencies they receive standalone Capabilities from this list, chosen by the Narrator.
Use by NPCs
Value (N): when a Capability uses the Level of its Competency, it is listed here with (N). The NPC's sheet gives that value in parentheses, from 1 to 5, such as Nothing Escapes (3). For the Capability's other rules, the NPC is treated as having the Competency at that Level.
Requirements: a Competency's common requirements, such as wielding a Shield, also apply to an NPC that has one of its Capabilities.
Dependencies: a Capability that depends on another only works if the NPC also has the other.
Equivalence: an NPC meant to have a Competency at a given Level receives the Capabilities up to that Level, with N equal to it. For example, a "Sentinel 2" guard receives Opportunity Attack and Halt.

regras/capacidades/capacidades-de-npc.text:
NPC Capabilities are Capabilities that only NPCs, creatures and enemies have access to. They belong to no Competency: the Narrator puts them directly on the NPC Sheet. NPCs can also receive Competency Capabilities as standalone Capabilities (see Use by NPCs).
Configurable values
Each NPC Capability comes with default values in parentheses, such as Potency, the Pool used to resist, the duration or the number of stacks. These values are configurable on each creature: two creatures with the same Capability can have different values.
Potency is the Difficulty of the test the target makes to resist, when the Capability calls for one.
When an NPC Capability mentions a Skill without spelling out the full Pool, it uses the Skill's linked Attribute. Pools expressly made of two Attributes, such as Vigor + Determination, stay unchanged.
When an NPC Capability does not set the Pool to resist, use Vigor + Determination against effects on the body and Determination + Cunning against effects on the mind.
Special movement
Swimming and climbing are Special Movement and cost 2 Movement points per square. With one of these Capabilities, the creature uses that movement at the normal cost, 1 point per square, and chooses on its Turn whether to spend its Movement on normal or special movement.
Aquatic and Flying can come with a value in parentheses, such as Aquatic (5): it is the creature's Movement in that medium, also at the normal cost. With no value, it uses its default Movement. A creature that only moves in water, such as a shark, has Movement 0 on land.
Aquatic
Description: swims at the normal cost and breathes underwater. With a value, swims with that Movement.
Flying
Description: flies at the normal cost (see Flight), with the value's Movement when there is one, and ignores Difficult Terrain on the ground. If it becomes Prone, Grappled or Paralyzed in the air, it falls.
Burrowing
Description: digs and moves through the earth at the normal cost. While buried, it cannot be the target of Attacks.
Climbing
Description: climbs walls and ceilings at the normal cost, without needing a test.
On-hit effects
When the creature wins an Attack with a melee natural Attack, the target makes a test to resist, with Difficulty equal to the Potency. On a failure, they suffer the effect.
Venomous (Potency 2; Vigor + Determination)
Description: a target who fails becomes Poisoned for a number of Turns equal to the Potency.
Paralyzing (Potency 2; Vigor + Strength)
Description: a target who fails becomes Paralyzed for 1 Turn.
Stunning (Potency 2; Determination + Cunning)
Description: a target who fails becomes Stunned for 1 Turn.
Infectious
Description: the disease or curse transmitted, the Pool to resist, the Potency and the duration are set on each creature (for example, lycanthropy).
Special attacks
Frenzy
Description: once per Turn, on winning an Attack, the creature makes another Attack against another target within its Reach, with -2 dice.
Improved Frenzy
Requirement: Frenzy
Description: Frenzy's extra Attack does not suffer the penalty.
Breath (Damage; Damage Type)
Description: with its Action, the creature creates an instant Zone in a Blast 3. The Zone has the Damage and Damage Type set on the creature. Breath cannot be used on consecutive Turns.
Charge (+2 Damage; 4 squares)
Description: if the creature moves at least 4 squares in a straight line before attacking, it adds +2 to the Damage of the Attack. It is the same rule as the weapon Property Charge, with its own values.
Go for the Throat (Margin 3)
Description: on winning an Attack with a Margin of 3 or more, the damage ignores the Absorption of the target's armor. Base Absorption and the armor's Resistances and Vulnerabilities still apply.
Constrictor (Margin 2)
Description: on winning an Attack with a Margin of 2 or more, the target also becomes Grappled. At the start of each of the creature's Turns, whoever it is grappling takes the Damage of its natural Attack.
Terrifying (Potency 2; Determination + Cunning; stacks equal to Potency)
Description: whoever sees the creature for the first time in the scene makes the test to resist. Whoever fails receives stacks of Fear.
Web (Potency 2; Range 6; Attack: Agility + Shooting; escape: Strength + Athletics)
Description: the creature makes a ranged Attack, up to the Range, with Agility + Shooting. A sheet can expressly set another Attack Attribute for its Web. On a win, it leaves the target Grappled by the web. To break free, the target uses their Action and tests Strength + Athletics against the Potency.
Burrowing Ambush
Requirement: Burrowing
Description: when coming out of the ground to attack, the creature tests Agility + Stealth against the target's Cunning + Perception. If it wins, it gets +2 dice on the Attack.
Swarm (damage by Size)
Description: the creature is a swarm of small critters, treated as a single one. At the start of each of its Turns, every creature in the space it occupies or adjacent to it takes superficial damage, with no Attack roll. The base damage comes from Size (Medium 2, Large 4, Huge 6) and drops by 1 for each creature hit beyond the first, to a minimum of 1. The creature's on-hit effects, such as Venomous, apply to each creature hit. The base damage can change on each creature. It is usually Immune to Slashing and Piercing.
Recovery
Regeneration (2; interrupted by the Damage Type or Material set on the creature)
Description: at the end of each of its Turns, the creature converts a number of points of aggravated damage to superficial equal to its Regeneration value, without needing treatment. The value is configurable on each creature.
Interruption: each creature lists the Damage Types or Materials that interrupt its Regeneration. If it took damage from one of them since the end of its last Turn, it does not regenerate on that Turn. The interruption lasts only that Turn: on the next Turn, with no new damage of that type, Regeneration comes back.
Senses
Darkvision (12 squares)
Description: up to its range, the creature treats Dim as Bright and Dark as Dim, but sees without telling colors apart. Beyond its range, Lighting applies as usual. Supernatural darkness blocks Darkvision.
regras/capacidades/capacidades-de-npc.html:
NPC Capabilities are Capabilities that only NPCs, creatures and enemies have access to. They belong to no Competency: the Narrator puts them directly on the NPC Sheet. NPCs can also receive Competency Capabilities as standalone Capabilities (see Use by NPCs).

Configurable values

Each NPC Capability comes with default values in parentheses, such as Potency, the Pool used to resist, the duration or the number of stacks. These values are configurable on each creature: two creatures with the same Capability can have different values.

Potency is the Difficulty of the test the target makes to resist, when the Capability calls for one.

When an NPC Capability mentions a Skill without spelling out the full Pool, it uses the Skill's linked Attribute. Pools expressly made of two Attributes, such as Vigor + Determination, stay unchanged.

When an NPC Capability does not set the Pool to resist, use Vigor + Determination against effects on the body and Determination + Cunning against effects on the mind.

Special movement

Swimming and climbing are Special Movement and cost 2 Movement points per square. With one of these Capabilities, the creature uses that movement at the normal cost, 1 point per square, and chooses on its Turn whether to spend its Movement on normal or special movement.

Aquatic and Flying can come with a value in parentheses, such as Aquatic (5): it is the creature's Movement in that medium, also at the normal cost. With no value, it uses its default Movement. A creature that only moves in water, such as a shark, has Movement 0 on land.

Aquatic

  • Description: swims at the normal cost and breathes underwater. With a value, swims with that Movement.

Flying

  • Description: flies at the normal cost (see Flight), with the value's Movement when there is one, and ignores Difficult Terrain on the ground. If it becomes Prone, Grappled or Paralyzed in the air, it falls.

Burrowing

  • Description: digs and moves through the earth at the normal cost. While buried, it cannot be the target of Attacks.

Climbing

  • Description: climbs walls and ceilings at the normal cost, without needing a test.

On-hit effects

When the creature wins an Attack with a melee natural Attack, the target makes a test to resist, with Difficulty equal to the Potency. On a failure, they suffer the effect.

Venomous (Potency 2; Vigor + Determination)

  • Description: a target who fails becomes Poisoned for a number of Turns equal to the Potency.

Paralyzing (Potency 2; Vigor + Strength)

  • Description: a target who fails becomes Paralyzed for 1 Turn.

Stunning (Potency 2; Determination + Cunning)

  • Description: a target who fails becomes Stunned for 1 Turn.

Infectious

  • Description: the disease or curse transmitted, the Pool to resist, the Potency and the duration are set on each creature (for example, lycanthropy).

Special attacks

Frenzy

  • Description: once per Turn, on winning an Attack, the creature makes another Attack against another target within its Reach, with -2 dice.

Improved Frenzy

  • Requirement: Frenzy
  • Description: Frenzy's extra Attack does not suffer the penalty.

Breath (Damage; Damage Type)

  • Description: with its Action, the creature creates an instant Zone in a Blast 3. The Zone has the Damage and Damage Type set on the creature. Breath cannot be used on consecutive Turns.

Charge (+2 Damage; 4 squares)

  • Description: if the creature moves at least 4 squares in a straight line before attacking, it adds +2 to the Damage of the Attack. It is the same rule as the weapon Property Charge, with its own values.

Go for the Throat (Margin 3)

  • Description: on winning an Attack with a Margin of 3 or more, the damage ignores the Absorption of the target's armor. Base Absorption and the armor's Resistances and Vulnerabilities still apply.

Constrictor (Margin 2)

  • Description: on winning an Attack with a Margin of 2 or more, the target also becomes Grappled. At the start of each of the creature's Turns, whoever it is grappling takes the Damage of its natural Attack.

regras/criaturas/ficha-de-npc.title: NPC Sheet
regras/criaturas/ficha-de-npc.summary: The NPC sheet is the simplified character sheet. It is used for human NPCs, such as a guard or a rival, and for creatures.
regras/criaturas/ficha-de-npc.text:
The NPC sheet is the simplified character sheet. It is used for human NPCs, such as a guard or a rival, and for creatures.
Fields
Field On the NPC sheet 
Name and Concept the Concept in one line 
Creature Type and Size as for characters 
Attributes from 1 to 5; creatures that are not human can go above 5 
Skills only those that are not 0 
Health 3 + Vigor (see Health) 
Willpower 3 + Determination (see Willpower) 
Initiative Cunning + Determination 
Movement 6, unless the sheet sets another value 
Absorption base Absorption and armor (see Absorption) 
Resistances, Vulnerabilities and Immunities as for characters 
Attacks weapons and natural Attacks 
Equipment chosen by the Narrator 
Capabilities standalone Capabilities, with their values in parentheses 
Ready Pools optional (see Ready Pools) 
Left off the sheet: Ambition, Desire, Convictions and Pillars, Maximum Load, XP, Competencies and Competency Points.
Instead of Competencies, the NPC receives standalone Capabilities, chosen by the Narrator from the Competency Capabilities and the NPC Capabilities (see Use by NPCs).
The NPC has no Maximum Load: the Narrator chooses equipment that fits it. If an NPC carries something clearly too heavy for the scene, the Narrator can apply Overload.
Health
The Health track follows the characters' rule: 3 + Vigor spaces. A creature that withstands more damage gets more Health in two ways:
Vigor above 5, for creatures that are not human. This also makes it more resistant to effects on the body, such as poisons.
Robust Body (N), which adds N spaces and changes nothing else.
Size does not change Health.
Willpower
Every NPC has a Willpower track of 3 + Determination spaces, as characters do, with all the Willpower rules, including the Capabilities that cost Willpower.
An NPC recovers superficial Willpower damage on a Long Rest. Aggravated damage is recovered when the Narrator decides, because the NPC has no Ambition or Convictions.
When the whole track is filled with aggravated damage, the Narrator sets the consequence, as in the Full Willpower rule. For NPCs, the most common one is to flee or surrender.
Absorption
Base Absorption is 0 by default. Thick hide, scales or a shell give base Absorption, with the value set on the sheet. Armor adds to it as for characters.
The sheet shows the total and where it comes from, such as "Absorption 3 (base 0, Breastplate 3)". Because it is base Absorption, natural protection does not penalize Dodge and is not ignored by Go for the Throat.
Natural Attacks
A natural Attack is an Attack made with the creature's body, such as claws, bites, horns or stingers. The sheet sets its Damage, Damage Type and Reach, like those of a weapon, and it uses Agility + Fighting, unless the sheet sets another Pool.
Origin: it has the Natural Origin: it does not take up the hands and cannot be Disarmed.
Material: it is Organic, unless the sheet sets another, such as the Common metal fists of an iron Construct.
Severity: it deals aggravated damage, as the general rule says. Unlike Unarmed, it is not superficial.
Properties: the sheet lists them as for a weapon. A Heavy natural Attack, for example, uses Strength + Fighting.
Grapple: the sheet can name a body part, such as the mouth or the tail, that counts as a free hand to Grapple. Without it, a creature without hands cannot Grapple.
Besides Capabilities, the sheet can define the creature's own attacks, such as a tail strike that creates a Zone. The sheet says what the attack does, with the same information a Capability would give: Action, shape, Damage and Damage Type.
Ready Pools
The sheet can list the most used Pools already added up, such as "Bite 5; Dodge 6", so the Narrator does not have to work them out during the scene. The rule is still Attribute + Skill: the line is only a note, and the scene's modifiers apply on top of it.
Progression
NPCs do not earn XP. An NPC who comes back stronger gets a new sheet, or one adjusted by the Narrator, within the Creating NPCs budget.
Template
Field Value 
Name Concept in one line 
Type and Size 
Attributes Str · Agi · Vig · Cha · Cun · Det 
Skills only those that are not 0 
Health · Willpower · Initiative · Movement · Absorption 
Resistances, Vulnerabilities and Immunities 
Attacks name, Damage, Damage Type, Reach and Properties 
Capabilities with their values in parentheses 
Equipment 
Ready Pools optional 
Examples
Wolf
Field Value 
Wolf pack hunter 
Type and Size Beast · Small 
Attributes Str 2 · Agi 3 · Vig 2 · Cha 1 · Cun 2 · Det 2 
Skills Acrobatics 3, Fighting 2, Perception 4 
Health · Willpower · Initiative · Movement · Absorption 5 · 5 · 4 · 8 · 0 
Attacks Bite, Damage 1, Piercing, Reach 1; grapples with its mouth 
Capabilities Go for the Throat (Margin 3) 
Ready Pools Bite 5; Dodge 6 
Orc Tribal Leader
Field Value 
Orc Tribal Leader warrior chief who leads through fear

regras/criaturas/criacao-de-npcs.summary: Creating NPCs is the budget the Narrator uses to build an NPC Sheet. It says how much an NPC can have at each tier, so the Narrator knows whether an enemy is a minion, an equal or a threat to the whole group, and so a…
regras/criaturas/criacao-de-npcs.text:
Creating NPCs is the budget the Narrator uses to build an NPC Sheet. It says how much an NPC can have at each tier, so the Narrator knows whether an enemy is a minion, an equal or a threat to the whole group, and so a strong Capability does not come cheaper to an NPC than to a character.
The budget is a reference, not an exact count: two NPCs of the same tier can have different strengths.
Tiers
Tier Equivalent to Attributes (sum; maximum) Skills (sum; maximum) Capability Points (maximum Level) Maximum natural Absorption 
Minion below a starting character 12; 3 8; 3 1 (Level 1) 1 
Peer a starting character 15; 4 18; 4 2 (Level 2) 2 
Veteran a character with about 30 XP 16; 5 22; 5 3 (Level 3) 3 
Elite a character with about 85 XP 17; 5 26; 5 5 (Level 4) 4 
Legendary beyond the characters 19 or more; above 5 for creatures that are not human 30; 5 8 (Level 5) 5 
Each tier's XP is the minimum Advancement cost for a starting character to reach it.
Capability Points
The NPC's standalone Capabilities come out of a single budget, the Capability Points:
Competency Capabilities: a Competency costs the highest Level the NPC has in it. Capabilities from Levels below it can be added at no extra cost. For example, Fury and Refuse to Fall cost 5, and a guard with Opportunity Attack and Halt costs 2.
Robust Body (N) costs N.
Maximum Level: the NPC cannot have a Competency Capability of a Level above its tier's maximum.
NPC Capabilities: cost as in the table below.
Cost NPC Capabilities 
0 Aquatic, Burrowing, Climbing, Darkvision, Infectious 
1 Flying, Frenzy, Improved Frenzy, Charge, Go for the Throat, Constrictor, Web, Burrowing Ambush, Venomous, Paralyzing, Stunning, Terrifying 
2 Breath, Swarm, Regeneration 
Each point of Potency above 2, each point of Regeneration above 2 and each point of Charge Damage above +2 costs +1. For example, Venomous (Potency 4) costs 3.
Breath Damage is set on the sheet. Because it is a Zone, it does not follow the natural Attack reference.
Natural Attacks
The Damage of a natural Attack follows the weapons' reference:
Base: 2, like a one-handed weapon; 1 for a Light natural Attack, such as the bite of a Small animal.
Size: +1 per category above Medium (Large 3, Huge 4, Colossal 5).
Damage does not go above this reference. The Heavy Property is free, as for weapons.
Health and Willpower
Health: Vigor is part of the Attribute sum, and Robust Body (N) costs N Capability Points.
Willpower: every NPC has a Willpower track, 3 + Determination, and Determination is part of the Attribute sum.
Encounters
A rule of thumb to build a scene:
1 Peer is a match for 1 character;
2 Minions equal 1 Peer;
1 Veteran is worth about 2 Peers;
1 Elite is worth about 3 Peers;
1 Legendary NPC is a challenge for the whole group.
An NPC on its own acts once per Round, while the group acts several times. That is why a Legendary NPC usually comes with Minions or Peers.

regras/criaturas/tipos-de-criatura.title: Creature Types
regras/criaturas/tipos-de-criatura.summary: The Creature Type classifies the nature of a character or creature. The default is Humanoid. The starting list of types is: Humanoid. Beast. Monstrosity. Undead. Construct. Elemental. Spirit. Aberration. Plant. Dragon…
regras/criaturas/tipos-de-criatura.text:
The Creature Type classifies the nature of a character or creature. The default is Humanoid.
The starting list of types is:
Humanoid
Beast
Monstrosity
Undead
Construct
Elemental
Spirit
Aberration
Plant
Dragon
Each creature has a single Type: the one that best describes what it is now. An undead dragon, for example, is Undead.
Creature Type only has an effect when a rule refers to it, such as the Hunter. Otherwise, it serves as a reference for the Narrator and as a basis for future rules, such as Capabilities, Resistances or effects that affect only certain types. Settings and modules can add new types and must say how the rules that refer to types treat them.
